findings.detail: Required active-role receipts lack authentic prompt, actual-context, spawn/session, start/end event, final-response, isolation/raw-export, and commit provenance. The v2 truth suite reports 63 missing/unavailable provenance fields. Hash equality and truthful nulls do not cure this; strategy §2.2 and A15 require a tool-attested, append-only superseding receipt chain.

All three browser records are audit-blocked because agent-browser was unavailable (probe exit 127); each remains runnable_disposition not-determined and reviewer disposition pending. Per strategy this is a B4 blocking audit limitation, not a non-runnable disposition. There are zero real-input events, transitions, console/network observations, or screenshots, and no screenshot/tooling bypass was accepted.

The implementation of BatchBIndependentReviewContract requires max(10, ceil(10%)) selected IDs even when a ledger contains fewer than ten factual claims. Archer's Revenge has eight claims, so the strategy's 'when enough exist' rule is satisfied by reviewing all eight but the test still fails. The truth-test owner must supersede the test contract rather than duplicate claims or invent two IDs.

The active discovery v2 package preserves original immutable bytes and confines DISC-001 to carried_forward_disclosures. Its append event/commit provenance remains unavailable and is already blocked by B-BLOCK-001.
